Class Database

java.lang.Object
database.Database
public class Database extends Object

Title: Database Class.

Description: This is an in-memory database built on H2. Detailed documentation of H2 can be found at https://www.h2database.com/html/main.html (Click on "PDF (2MP) for a PDF of 438 pages on the H2 main page.) This class leverages H2 and provides numerous special supporting methods.

    • getPostsByThread

      public List<Post> getPostsByThread(int threadId)

      Method: List<Post>; getPostsByThread(int threadId)

      Description: Returns ALL Posts belonging to the given thread (including soft-deleted ones), ordered by timestamp ascending so students read the conversation in chronological order. Soft-deleted posts are included so their replies remain accessible; the caller should check Post.isDeleted() and display a placeholder instead of the content.

      Parameters:
      threadId - the threadId whose Posts should be retrieved
      Returns:
      a List of Post objects (active and deleted); empty if the thread has no posts

    • getPostsByAuthor

      public List<Post> getPostsByAuthor(String username)

      Method: List<Post>; getPostsByAuthor(String username)

      Description: Returns ALL Posts written by the given user (including soft-deleted ones), ordered by timestamp descending (newest first) so the student sees their most recent content at the top. Soft-deleted posts are included so the student can see their full history; the caller should check Post.isDeleted() and mark them accordingly.

      Parameters:
      username - the authorUsername to filter on
      Returns:
      a List of Post objects (active and deleted); empty if the user has no posts

    • searchPosts

      public List<Post> searchPosts(String keyword, int threadId)

      Method: List<Post>; searchPosts(String keyword, int threadId)

      Description: Returns non-deleted Posts whose content contains the given keyword (case-insensitive substring match). If threadId is -1, all threads are searched; otherwise only the specified thread is searched. Results are ordered by timestamp descending so the most recent matches appear first.

      Parameters:
      keyword - the search term; the query uses LOWER(content) LIKE ? so the match is case-insensitive
      threadId - the thread to restrict the search to, or -1 to search all threads
      Returns:
      a List of matching Post objects; empty if no matches are found

    • getRepliesForPost

      public List<Reply> getRepliesForPost(int postId)

      Method: List<Reply>; getRepliesForPost(int postId)

      Description: Returns all Replies for the given postId, ordered by timestamp ascending so the conversation thread reads in chronological order. Soft-deleted replies are included so their position in the thread is preserved; the caller should check Reply.isDeleted() and display a placeholder instead of the content.

      Parameters:
      postId - the postId whose Replies should be retrieved
      Returns:
      a List of Reply objects (including soft-deleted); empty if the post has no replies

    • getUnreadReplyCount

      public int getUnreadReplyCount(int postId, String username)

      Method: int getUnreadReplyCount(int postId, String username)

      Description: Returns the number of replies to the given post that the specified user has not yet read. A reply is "unread" if there is no matching row in the ReadStatus table with targetType = 'reply' for this user.

      Parameters:
      postId - the postId whose replies are examined
      username - the viewer whose ReadStatus rows are checked
      Returns:
      the count of unread replies (0 if all have been read or there are no replies)

    • markPostAsRead

      public void markPostAsRead(int postId, String username)

      Method: void markPostAsRead(int postId, String username)

      Description: Records that the given user has read the given post. The operation is idempotent: calling it multiple times does not create duplicate rows because the UNIQUE constraint on (username, targetId, targetType) turns the INSERT into a no-op via H2's MERGE statement.

      Parameters:
      postId - the postId to mark as read
      username - the user marking the post as read

    • updatePost

      public int updatePost(int postId, String newContent, String authorUsername)

      Method: int updatePost(int postId, String newContent, String authorUsername)

      Description: Updates the content of a non-deleted Post, but only if the row belongs to authorUsername. The author check is performed inside the WHERE clause, so an unprivileged user who guesses a postId cannot overwrite someone else's post. Returns the number of rows updated (1 on success; 0 if the post does not exist, is soft-deleted, or the requester is not the author).

      Parameters:
      postId - the postId to update
      newContent - the replacement content; should be pre-validated by PostContentRecognizer
      authorUsername - the username of the student attempting the edit
      Returns:
      1 if the update succeeded; 0 otherwise

    • softDeletePost

      public int softDeletePost(int postId, String authorUsername)

      Method: int softDeletePost(int postId, String authorUsername)

      Description: Sets isDeleted = TRUE for the given Post, but only if the row belongs to authorUsername. Replies attached to a soft-deleted post are kept intact; the UI should display a "(post deleted)" notice in place of the original content. Returns the number of rows updated (1 on success; 0 if not found or wrong author).

      Parameters:
      postId - the postId to soft-delete
      authorUsername - the username of the student attempting the deletion
      Returns:
      1 if the post was soft-deleted; 0 otherwise

    • softDeleteReply

      public int softDeleteReply(int replyId, String authorUsername)

      Method: int softDeleteReply(int replyId, String authorUsername)

      Description: Sets isDeleted = TRUE for the given Reply, but only if the row belongs to authorUsername. The row is never physically removed; the UI should display a "[Reply deleted]" notice in place of the original content. Returns the number of rows updated (1 on success; 0 if not found or wrong author).

      Parameters:
      replyId - the replyId to soft-delete
      authorUsername - the username of the student attempting the deletion
      Returns:
      1 if the reply was soft-deleted; 0 otherwise

    • updateReply

      public int updateReply(int replyId, String newContent, String authorUsername)

      Method: int updateReply(int replyId, String newContent, String authorUsername)

      Description: Updates the content of a non-deleted Reply, but only if the row belongs to authorUsername. The author check and the isDeleted guard are both performed inside the WHERE clause, so an unprivileged user cannot overwrite someone else's reply and deleted replies cannot be edited. Returns the number of rows updated (1 on success; 0 if the reply does not exist, is soft-deleted, or the requester is not the author).

      Parameters:
      replyId - the replyId to update
      newContent - the replacement content; should be pre-validated by PostContentRecognizer
      authorUsername - the username of the student attempting the edit
      Returns:
      1 if the update succeeded; 0 otherwise

    • seedDefaultThread

      public void seedDefaultThread() throws SQLException

      Method: seedDefaultThread

      Description: Inserts the "General" discussion thread if it does not already exist. This method is called once from FoundationsMain.start() after the database tables have been created, ensuring that there is always at least one thread available for students to post into. Using INSERT IGNORE (H2: INSERT INTO ... WHERE NOT EXISTS) means the call is safely idempotent — running it multiple times does not produce duplicate rows.

      Throws:
      SQLException - if the INSERT statement fails for a reason other than the row already existing

    • createPost

      public int createPost(Post post) throws SQLException

      Method: int createPost(Post post)

      Description: Inserts a new Post row into the Posts table and returns the auto-generated postId. The generated key is also written back into the Post object via post.setPostId() so the caller can reference it immediately (e.g., to display "Your post was created with ID: X" or to chain a reply). The method validates that the referenced threadId exists before attempting the INSERT. If the thread is not found a SQLException is thrown with a descriptive message rather than letting the foreign-key constraint produce a less readable error.

      Parameters:
      post - the Post object to persist; must have threadId, authorUsername, content, and timestamp populated; postId may be 0 (it will be set by this method)
      Returns:
      the auto-generated postId assigned by the database
      Throws:
      SQLException - if the threadId does not exist, the INSERT fails, or no generated key is returned

      public int createReply(Reply reply) throws SQLException

      Method: int createReply(Reply reply)

      Description: Inserts a new Reply row into the Replies table and returns the auto-generated replyId. The generated key is also written back into the Reply object via reply.setReplyId(). The method validates that the referenced postId exists before attempting the INSERT. If the post is not found a SQLException is thrown with a descriptive message. Note that replies are allowed on soft-deleted posts (isDeleted = TRUE); the soft-delete flag only affects content visibility, not the ability to reply.

      Parameters:
      reply - the Reply object to persist; must have postId, authorUsername, content, and timestamp populated; replyId may be 0 (it will be set by this method)
      Returns:
      the auto-generated replyId assigned by the database
      Throws:
      SQLException - if the postId does not exist, the INSERT fails, or no generated key is returned

    • getRequestHistory

      public List<Request> getRequestHistory(int requestId)

      Method: List<Request> getRequestHistory(int requestId)

      Description: Returns the full history chain for a request. If requestId is the original closed request, the result includes that row and every reopened descendant. If requestId refers to a reopened request, the method first resolves its originalClosedRequestId and then returns the full chain anchored at that original request. Results are ordered by creation time ascending so the history reads oldest-to-newest.

      Parameters:
      requestId - the original or reopened request ID whose history should be retrieved
      Returns:
      a chronologically ordered list of related request rows; empty if the anchor is invalid

    • reopenClosedRequest

      public int reopenClosedRequest(String staffUsername, String title, String description, int originalClosedRequestId) throws SQLException

      Method: int reopenClosedRequest(String staffUsername, String title, String description, int originalClosedRequestId)

      Description: Creates a brand-new OPEN request row that represents a reopened version of a previously closed request. The original request is never overwritten. Instead, the new row stores the original request ID in originalClosedRequestId so the system preserves history and allows callers to navigate back to the original closed request. Input validation is performed before insertion: title must satisfy TitleRecognizer, description must satisfy PostContentRecognizer, the originalClosedRequestId must refer to an existing CLOSED request, and staffUsername must belong to a user with the Staff role.

      Parameters:
      staffUsername - the staff user reopening the request
      title - the updated title for the reopened request
      description - the updated description for the reopened request
      originalClosedRequestId - the original closed request to link back to
      Returns:
      the generated requestId for the new reopened request
      Throws:
      SQLException - if validation fails or the INSERT fails
